## F1 — P2: An empty replacement transcript leaves superseded history visible

**Confidence: high; reproduced through the real delta builder.**

Locations: [internal/cli/history_delta.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_delta.go:597), [internal/cli/history_delta.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_delta.go:657), [internal/cli/history_delta.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_delta.go:696), and [internal/cli/history_delta.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_delta.go:468). The brief path also checks replacement-row count at [internal/cli/agent_surface.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/agent_surface.go:1582).

`loadFreshHistoryOverlay` records a changed path in `fresh.replaced` even if its replacement contains zero records. Several consumers then treat `len(fresh.overlay) == 0` as proof that there is no replacement to apply. They return the old long-term records without honoring that path set.

The reproduction created an indexed transcript, replaced its contents with an empty file, and ran the actual short-term builder. The builder reported `Files:1 Records:0 Scanned:1 Failed:0`; the merged view still contained all three old records. Unified lexical retrieval returned the removed decision with no error, `VerificationRequired:false`, and no caveats. A smaller diagnostic also demonstrated that merged, active, and ranked views each retain a superseded record.

**Consequence:** content removed from a transcript can remain visible until consolidation. This is a freshness defect; the audit does not claim a bypass of the separate session-tombstone privacy mechanism.

**Graph evidence:** `mergedRecords` feeds `reconciledRecords` and conversation session views; `longTermActive` feeds semantic retrieval through `longTermReconciled`; `rankFreshHistory` feeds brief, history, and conversation retrieval. See [merged-view impact](/Users/thomi/.codex/visualizations/2026/09/18/01a0b6ce-e2ad-7853-bb2f-19731062a2c9/code-quality-audit/evidence/audit-impact-merged.txt), [active-view impact](/Users/thomi/.codex/visualizations/2026/09/18/01a0b6ce-e2ad-7853-bb2f-19731062a2c9/code-quality-audit/evidence/audit-impact-active.txt), and [ranking impact](/Users/thomi/.codex/visualizations/2026/09/18/01a0b6ce-e2ad-7853-bb2f-19731062a2c9/code-quality-audit/evidence/audit-impact-rankfresh.txt).

**Recommended remedy:** distinguish “no replacement paths” from “replacement paths with no rows,” and honor replacement membership in every view and fast path. Add coverage for a successful zero-record rescan, alongside the existing no-delta and nonempty-replacement tests.



## F2 — P2: Filtering replaced records after top-N selection loses valid matches

**Confidence: high; reproduced with the production scorer.**

Location: [internal/cli/history_delta.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_delta.go:688).

`rankFreshHistory` first obtains a bounded long-term result list, then removes records superseded by the overlay. It never refills the surviving list from lower-ranked eligible records. If the selected records all belong to replaced files and the new contents do not match, the result can be empty despite matching unaffected history.

The reproduction used three matching old records, two in a replaced file and one in an unaffected file, with a limit of two. Current ranking returned zero rows; ranking the eligible records returned the unaffected match. Some callers over-fetch, but a fixed reserve only moves the threshold at which this happens. The main brief path passes its requested limit directly.

**Consequence:** false negatives in retrieval, including misleading absence of recorded context.

**Graph evidence:** the shared ranker has production callers in unified retrieval, conversation retrieval, brief generation, and focused brief history. See [ranking impact](/Users/thomi/.codex/visualizations/2026/09/18/01a0b6ce-e2ad-7853-bb2f-19731062a2c9/code-quality-audit/evidence/audit-impact-rankfresh.txt). The impact report also includes tests; its aggregate caller count is not a count of distinct product features.

**Recommended remedy:** apply replacement eligibility during candidate selection or refill by paging until the requested number of eligible results is reached or the candidates are exhausted. Preserve the existing on-disk FTS identity; simply rebuilding FTS from a merged slice would violate another established constraint.



## F5 — P2: Fact retrieval rebuilds the same review graph within one request

**Confidence: high for redundant work; runtime impact not benchmarked.**

Locations: [internal/cli/retrieve.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/retrieve.go:269), [internal/cli/retrieval_guard.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/retrieval_guard.go:162), [internal/cli/retrieval_guard.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/retrieval_guard.go:183), and [internal/cli/retrieval_guard.go](/Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/5d33/entire-brain/internal/cli/retrieval_guard.go:46).

The ordinary fact retrieval path calls `guardedFactCandidateLimit`, which builds the proposal components, then calls `guardUnifiedFactResults`, which builds them again. Even with no proposals, `buildFactReviewGroups` first allocates and populates a map of active facts before returning no groups. The guard separately builds another full fact map. `indexFactReviewGroups` also builds an ID index that this caller discards.

**Consequence:** avoidable corpus-sized scans and allocations for small result pages, including the common no-review path. The union-find algorithm itself has a reasonable purpose; the repeated construction is the problem.

**Graph evidence:** both helpers call `buildFactReviewGroups`; unified retrieval invokes both helpers. See [grouping impact](/Users/thomi/.codex/visualizations/2026/09/18/01a0b6ce-e2ad-7853-bb2f-19731062a2c9/code-quality-audit/evidence/audit-impact-buildgroups.txt) and [candidate-limit impact](/Users/thomi/.codex/visualizations/2026/09/18/01a0b6ce-e2ad-7853-bb2f-19731062a2c9/code-quality-audit/evidence/audit-impact-factgroups.txt).

**Recommended remedy:** return early for no proposals, prepare the review groups once per request, and construct only the lookup maps the caller needs. Preserve full-branch membership semantics and stable review IDs.



## F32 — P2 — Document get hides a missing declared index

`internal/cli/retrieve.go:1210–1223` ignores os.IsNotExist from loadDocIndex without checking the manifest. After an indexed document file is deleted, query reports a storage defect, but get/multi-get reports an ordinary missing ID. Users/clients cannot distinguish data loss from an unknown ID at the expansion step. Apply the existing declared-index distinction to document ID retrieval. TestAuditGetLostDeclaredDocs in audit-retrieval-repro.log reproduces the divergence. Graph getUnifiedBatchOptions impact: 10 direct + 20 transitive callers incl CLI/workspace/MCP. Brain getdoc retrieval returned history-gap summaries of source availability reviews; these are incomplete historical context, not proof of current behavior.



## F34 — P2 — Fused history evaluation ranks failed embeddings as semantic matches

`internal/cli/history_eval.go:459–535` accepts zero, nil, and wrong-dimension candidate embeddings. A zero cosine still earns a semantic reciprocal-rank contribution, producing successful ranked results for unrelated records when no lexical match exists. TestAuditHistoryEvalFailedCandidateEmbedding reproduces an unrelated decision returned after candidate embedding failure (`audit-historyeval-repro.log`). Validate embedding shape/finite norm and surface unavailable evaluation arms rather than scoring a failed signal. Graph selectHistoryEvalArm identifies the CLI evaluation connection (3 direct + 1 transitive callers); method-value dispatch is not fully represented by the rank method's callers. Brain retrieved the semantic evaluation plan but no specific justification for accepting failed candidate vectors.

### Further stale comment/test examples

- `history_input.go:41–49` says historySessionInventoryError deliberately does not unwrap, but its Unwrap method is directly below. The error-chain explanation is false.
- `doc_contract_test.go:83` says vsearch advertises neither option while assertions require the shared schema.
- `doc_fts.go:143` names rankDocsViaFTS above rankDocsLexical.
- Document-vector repair tests share the invalid-cache seed problem: savePresent discards the zero vector before retrieval sees it.



## F35 — P2 — Index-backed FTS ranking mixes generations during refresh

`internal/cli/history_fts.go:817–868` checks cache freshness in openHistoryFTS, then queries outside that check's read transaction. A concurrent rebuild can change rec_order between those operations; the ranker uses the new order against its old in-memory index, returning unrelated old records. The exhaustive ranker has the same separation. An external Go overlay adds only a deterministic scheduling hook after open and commits another generation before the query; querying “quasar” then returns the old “unrelated banana” record (`audit-ftsrace-repro.log`). This is a schedule-controlled reproduction, not a stress-test frequency estimate. Bind freshness and ranking to one read snapshot, as the direct-payload path already does. Graph filtered ranker impact: 5 direct + 51 transitive callers, including conversation and unified retrieval; Brain retrieval found general transactional-generation guidance but no specific rationale for this gap.

Code relationships — callers, callees, dependents, implementors, type consumers,
routes, and blast radius — MUST be answered with Graph first, ALWAYS, even when
the task names the exact file or you have already read the implementation.
Use neighbors for a specific relationship and impact for blast radius.
Grep may supplement a Graph answer; it NEVER replaces the required Graph query.

ALWAYS run impact before editing exported code or shared-library symbols.
Writing a spec, scoping a refactor, reviewing a proposed change, and challenging
a design count as editing for this rule. Cover every affected exported or
shared-library symbol and cite its impact result. Do not infer that a change
is local merely because its implementation occupies one file.

Use Graph diff, commit, or checkpoint for entity-level revision comparisons.
Read the textual diff as needed to inspect the implementation.

Text occurrences the graph does not model — environment-variable names,
configuration values, string keys, and package-manifest entries — belong in
text search. One legitimate text search does not authorize using grep to answer
a relationship question.

ALWAYS use --head for interactive Graph queries by default, including the first
query. Use the working tree ONLY when the answer depends on uncommitted edits;
then omit --head. Working-tree queries rebuild the snapshot on every call and
never cache; --head permits reuse of the committed-tree cache. Never present
committed-tree results as analysis of edits they do not contain.
Before several --head queries, prewarm the matching cache variant.
Ask per-symbol commands before bulk streams. Never dump unfiltered whole-repo
NDJSON into context; redirect it to a file and extract the needed records.

An empty Graph result is NEVER proof of no consumers. Check completeness,
resolution, and confidence. Verify heuristic relationships in focused source.
For dependency injection, inspect type consumers as well as CALLS. Check
dynamic dispatch and unmodeled relationships with targeted supplementary
inspection. State unresolved coverage limits in the answer.

Both sets of mandatory rules apply.
Brain answers recorded-context and historical questions; Graph answers structural
questions and entity-level revision comparisons.

## F38 evaluation protocol (frozen before reading results)

Read-only local corpus inputs: the single history generation in each of the `entireio/entire-brain` and `entireio/entire-graph` Brain stores. For each transcript path, sort records by anchor line, take the first indexed request as query and subsequent general-rankable record IDs as provenance labels. Keep 2–200 labels, SHA256(path)[0] modulo 5 == 0, sort by full hash, cap at 24 per repository. Score the full frozen index with the production substring history ranker at k=10. No parameter fitting: variant removes only topic-specific +80/+90/-60 exceptions, retaining all existing generic evidence heuristics. Report hit@10, MRR@10, mean provenance recall@10 and paired task changes. No prompts or raw transcript text are emitted in evidence; task hashes and result IDs only.

Evaluator source retained outside repo as `evidence/f38-evaluator.go`. It is an offline opt-in probe, not a production fixture or permanent release benchmark. Corpus SHA256s are logged, and unchanged corpus hashes must match across arms. The sample is held out from this remediation's rule selection; the historical tuning lineage is unknown, so this does not establish that original authors never saw these sessions. Provenance labels are only a proxy for answer usefulness; small sample and low recall do not support a global recall-quality claim.

Baseline run hit the default ten-minute test timeout after 22 completed tasks (`f38-heldout-baseline.log`). The immutable task list is resumed using completed hash IDs (`f38-heldout-baseline-resume.log`), not reduced based on outcomes. Aggregate evaluation uses unique per-task log rows across parts, never partial resume summaries. This timeout is a workload limit of the offline corpus probe, not a failing product regression.
EOF

## F12 — P2: Pending proposals accept withdrawn replacements

internal/factmerge/admin.go:28 checks that both IDs exist but not their statuses. Retract a candidate while its supersede proposal remains pending, then apply the proposal: the active target becomes superseded by the retracted candidate, leaving neither active. Retained retired records make existence insufficient as a stale-state check. Validate applicability against current statuses before mutating. The same boundary also accepts self-merge proposals and deletes their sole fact; unknown actions fall through to supersede. Graph follows this helper into CLI review and hosted ResolveOpen. Evidence: audit-extra-repro.log and audit-impact-proposal.txt. Ordinary stale-status handling is the primary finding; malformed self-proposals are additional boundary cases.



## F28 — P2: Manual fact updates falsely certify distillation coverage

`internal/cli/blind_spot.go:22` treats `Sources.Facts.GeneratedAt` as the last distillation time. `facts_manifest.go:112` updates it to now for remember, review, gc and reclassification, including a no-op refresh reclassification. In a fixture with two captured sessions and no distillation, calling the same manifest updater used by those commands changes the empty-result note to “all captured sessions are distilled.” This can discourage needed processing and misrepresent absent knowledge. Track actual processing coverage independently of fact-store refresh time; do not claim all sessions are processed based solely on their creation timestamps. Graph identifies empty-result retrieval and handoff consumers and fourteen consumers of the preservation helper. Brain retrieved the original blind-spot requirement in semantic_brain_plan.md:1206, which asks for actual undigested-session coverage. Reproduction: `audit-coverage-repro.log`.

The same preservation helper drops `TokenUsage` while retaining the other prior-run metrics. A second assertion confirms token accounting disappears on administrative manifest rebuilds. Preserve the complete last-run evidence as a unit rather than manually copying an expanding list of fields.



## F29 — P2: Negative tree leaf limit crashes the CLI

`internal/cli/facts_tree.go:154` slices with the unvalidated `--leaves` value. `facts tree --leaves -1` on a nonempty branch panics instead of returning a flag error. The overlay reproduces this through the real root command and a normal stored fact. Validate numeric options before retrieval/rendering. Graph confirms the command-to-renderer path; Brain retrieval found general tree/expansion design but no reason to allow this input. Evidence: `audit-factinputs-repro.log`.

A separate, lower-priority parser robustness issue exists in `facts_expand.go:77`: reading a cache containing valid JSON `null` sets its map to nil, then the next successful expansion panics assigning into that map. The same overlay reproduces it. Normalize decoded cache state and handle malformed cache inputs deliberately. Graph traces persistent cache loading to facts eval; ordinary recall uses an in-memory empty-path cache.

### Comment quality: false certainty and repetition

`facts_integrity.go` spends its first 83 lines retelling corruption incidents before declaring a type, and repeats the same accounts on fields and individual branches. Its duplicated-ID warning asserts every duplicate replaced a different fact, although a duplicate may simply have been appended (the code later acknowledges that case). `facts_admin_cmd.go` and its flag-validation tests likewise repeat the claim that promoting into a nonexistent branch destroys facts, although the source branch remains and explicit branch lookup can access the new store. Keep the actionable validation and corruption checks; replace these narratives with concise, accurate invariants. `facts_sync_cmd.go:324` also leaves a stale reconcileLocalProposalQueue comment attached to readSharedFactHead.



## F30 — P2: Resolving a hosted proposal can modify a different local repository

`internal/cli/facts_proposals_cmd.go:323` invokes local settlement after a successful hosted resolution without passing or verifying the hosted repository identity. `pruneLocalProposalCopy` selects the current checkout solely from Options and matches content-derived fact IDs. Run `facts proposals apply ... --repo-id <other-repository>` from a checkout containing the same facts: the command supersedes that checkout's local fact too, even with no local shared-proposal entry. An end-to-end CLI overlay with the existing loopback fake reproduces the wrong local status change. Require an established mapping between the hosted target and local store before mirroring; otherwise report the hosted outcome without mutating an unrelated checkout. Graph traces the resolver into this helper. Brain retrieved the original local queue-pruning change but no cross-repository binding requirement. Evidence: `audit-proposalrepo-repro.log`.

Additional test-quality example: `facts_test.go:11` names path-order stability, but its first two calls pass paths in exactly the same order. Reverse one input to exercise the stated property. The alias-level merge tests largely repeat the merge-core tests; preserve CLI integration assertions when consolidating.



## F31 — P2 — Standard silver fact-evaluation output cannot be compared by default

`internal/cli/facts_eval.go:842–861` emits `labeled=false` and `provenance_silver_label` for fixed silver task labels. `facts_eval_compare.go:266–275` requires `labeled=true` and `explicit_label`, rejecting even a summary compared with itself as “different ground truths.” `history_eval.go:382–391` represents the same label grade differently and passes. This contradicts the comparator comment and the recorded same-truth/non-proof distinction. Normalize the representation/comparability of fixed labels independently from release evidence grade, and test the facts gen→eval→compare seam as well as history. Repro: `evidence/audit-eval-repro.log`, TestAuditSilverOutputComparison. Graph impact: comparator 1 direct + 5 transitive callers (`audit-impact-evallabels.json`). Brain: release-blockers.md R1 at retained line 50 and session history:6426eca537eeaecb0cb9865f line 3965 document the intended distinction; release_readiness_audit.md has conflicting older strict wording, so source plus reproduction establishes current behavior.



## F49 — P2: secret-field redaction misses common quoting formats
`redaction.go:18` assumes the secret name immediately precedes the separator and consumes only a non-whitespace value. Quoted JSON keys (`{"API_KEY":"REDACTED"}` and `{"password": "REDACTED"}`) and `PASSWORD='audit fake credential value'` survive unchanged. TestAuditQuotedJSONSecretSurvivesRedaction uses fabricated credentials only. This affects the pattern evidence egress boundary, drafts and other redacted artifacts. Handle quoted keys and quoted values, with tests against actual serialized evidence. Graph redactText: 44 direct/67 transitive callers. Brain reference/threat-model docs describe best-effort redaction; that limitation does not explain missing the routine formats for explicitly supported field names. Evidence audit-redact*.



## F50 — P2: failure-tail hook reads the wrong end of large logs
`hook_cmd.go:294–302` applies a 1 MiB LimitReader before taking the last 4096 bytes. For larger logs, the true final errors are never read; it instead matches the end of the first MiB. TestAuditHookDropsActualFailureTail proves a final failure marker disappears. Use bounded-memory tail buffering through EOF, with appropriate cancellation, or require and accurately document pre-truncated input. Graph and Brain evidence audit-hooktail*; reproduction in audit-redact-repro.log.

### More comment quality issues
`reconcile_test.go` TestParseReconcileActionsRejectsNaNConfidence describes a new-line confidence default but actually tests merge confidence zero. `reconcile.go` writeFactProposals says deduplication uses a triple, while dedupeProposals correctly uses five fields; the following 12-line repair narrative can be reduced to the shared identity invariant. `redaction.go` claims every evidence field passes through a no-secrets boundary more strongly than the implementation establishes.



## F51 — P2: NaN confidence bypasses review and fails only after writes
`distill_cmd.go:614` checks only <=0 and >1, admitting NaN; runDistillForBrain passes it into the threshold comparison. `TestAuditDistillNaNThresholdAppliesLowConfidence` reproduces automatic supersession at confidence 0.01 and then a manifest JSON encoding error for NaN, after the fact store has changed. Reject non-finite configuration at both CLI and engine boundaries before calls or writes; parser guards already do this for model-produced confidence. External reproduction uses the engine; CLI admission is established by the flag predicate. Graph runDistillForBrain covers the production CLI and library consumers. Evidence audit-distillnew* and audit-distill-impact/brain.



## F52 — P2: distillation replaces newer session manifests with its old snapshot
`distill_cmd.go:1284–1288` publishes the manifest loaded at the beginning of a potentially hours-long pass. The final writer lock protects only that write and does not merge changes since the earlier read. TestAuditDistillOverwritesNewSessionManifest writes a newly captured session under the same brain lock during an agent call; successful distillation removes it from the manifest. Reload the current manifest inside the final lock and update only the fact-source fields owned by this pass. Reproduction audit-distillnew*; Graph runDistillForBrain impact retained. Existing concurrent-writer tests cover facts but omit manifest sources.



## F53 — P2: proposal read errors become destructive queue replacement
`distill_cmd.go:1002–1017` logs loadFactProposals errors and proceeds with an empty prior queue. `writeFactProposals` then replaces or removes the old file. TestAuditDistillErasesMalformedProposalQueue shows a malformed existing queue deleted by a successful incremental distill. Refuse publication on unreadable queue state; preserve the evidence for repair. Graph loadFactProposals and runDistillForBrain impact retained. Evidence audit-distillnew* and audit-proposalread*.

### Distillation maintenance issues
- runDistillForBrain combines scheduling, extraction, reconciliation, cache migration, rebase, publication and reporting in roughly 540 lines with several large closures. Its concurrency fixes protect individual facts but the final manifest still has a stale-snapshot gap (F52); explicit phase/result types and a single publication transaction would make ownership reviewable. The pipeline's ordered dispatcher is justified by its deadlock invariant; preserve that invariant during any refactor.
- `distillSessionFingerprint` first says it hashes transcript path, then says it deliberately does not. `concurrency` refers to removed chunkPrefetcher. `saveDistillCache` calls failure non-fatal even though final flush returns it. `parseDocumentConversation` says tool outputs are scanned past, but ToolOutputs now materializes them.
- Numerous comments narrate previous failures and observed corpus sizes at length. Keep current invariants, compatibility boundaries and non-obvious scheduling rationale; move incident chronology to history/docs.



## F54 — P2: distill cache and proposal readers can block indefinitely on FIFOs
`distill_cmd.go` loadDistillCache and `reconcile.go` loadFactProposals call os.ReadFile directly, bypassing the bounded regular-file state reader immediately above the cache loader. TestAuditDistillAndProposalFIFOBlock confirms both block until a controlled writer arrives. The reads have no context or byte bound, and proposal reads also occur inside the brain writer lock. Use the existing safe state-reader boundary and preserve meaningful errors for non-rebuildable queue state. Graph cache loader 16 direct/51 transitive callers; proposal loader 27 direct/76 transitive. Evidence audit-statefifo*, audit-distillcache-impact and audit-proposalread-impact. Same boundary class as F37; consolidate in final prioritization without hiding affected consumers.

### Further distill test gaps
- TestExecDistillAgentTimesOutAndKillsTheProcess checks absence of a marker after about five seconds even though the marker is scheduled after 30 seconds; it does not establish the claimed lifetime property. The separate inherited-pipe test does verify wait duration and cleans up its child.
- TestForcedCappedDistillDoesNotStrandDeferredSessions uses recordingDistillRunner, which emits invalid two-level taxonomy `conventions.testing`. It proves cache visitation but creates no facts, despite claiming to prove preservation/recovery of dropped facts.
- TestInProcessDistillOptionsPassTheConcurrencyGuard describes both watcher and session-end coverage but asserts watcher options only.
- Brain doc:a01f73bf7558 explicitly says source owners must not independently replace shared manifest state (F52); doc:c31974aa0661 defines the low-confidence review contract (F51).

# Facts audit remediation

Branch codex/audit2-facts, base c6dff964. All eleven assigned findings reproduced and fixed.

| Finding | Change and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| F12 | Reject inactive records, self proposals, and unsupported actions before mutation. f12-red.log fails on old behavior; f12-green.log passes full factmerge/factsync suites. |
| F28 | Record LastDistilledAt only from actual distillation; preserve timestamp and token usage across manual updates. Empty results describe unknown coverage rather than inferring completeness from timestamps. f28-red.log and f28-green.log; manual timestamp/usage persistence regression included. Legacy manifests without a run timestamp remain explicitly unknown. |
| F29 | Reject negative tree leaves before resolving storage; rebuild null/malformed expansion cache maps. f29-red.log/f29-green.log, both text and JSON flag paths and persisted cache reuse. |
| F30 | Record successful HTTP sync's repo/API binding per branch; verify under local writer lock before mirroring hosted settlements. Missing or mismatched binding leaves facts/queue untouched and warns; successful real sync followed by proposal apply still mirrors. f30-red.log and f30-f31-green.log cover missing/different repo/different API and matching sync. |
| F31 | Compare actual fixed provenance-silver evaluator results without falsely upgrading their evidence grade. Partial/mixed silver remains noncomparable. f31-red.log/f30-f31-green.log includes real evaluator to comparator flow. |
| F49 | Redact JSON quoted secret keys and complete quoted values including whitespace, escapes and unterminated quotes. f49-f50-red.log/green.log. Clarify scope of redaction comment. |
| F50 | Stream through EOF with bounded retained memory, returning the actual final diagnostic after multi-megabyte output. f49-f50-red.log/green.log. |
| F51 | Reject NaN/infinite confidence before agents or writes; preserve existing default threshold handling. f51-f53-red.log/green.log. |
| F52 | Reload the manifest while holding the final write lock so concurrent session exports survive. f51-f53-red.log/green.log uses a real concurrent writer between extraction and publication. |
| F53 | Pre-read every dirty branch's proposal queue before any flush writes; return parse/read failures without destroying queue evidence. f51-f53-red.log/green.log preserves malformed original bytes. |
| F54 | Read distill cache/proposals through bounded hardened state reader, rejecting FIFO/symlink hazards. Rebuildable cache fails empty; durable queue errors propagate. f54-red.log/green.log controls and unblocks FIFO regression. |

Brain brief and retained rationale are in brief.json/history-context.json; source index is stale so retained context was used only for rationale. The same boundary also accepts self-merge proposals and deletes their sole fact; unknown actions fall through to supersede. Graph follows this helper into CLI review and hosted ResolveOpen. Evidence: audit-extra-repro.log and audit-impact-proposal.txt. Ordinary stale-status handling is the primary finding; malformed self-proposals are additional boundary cases.



## F28 — P2: Manual fact updates falsely certify distillation coverage

`internal/cli/blind_spot.go:22` treats `Sources.Facts.GeneratedAt` as the last distillation time. `facts_manifest.go:112` updates it to now for remember, review, gc and reclassification, including a no-op refresh reclassification. In a fixture with two captured sessions and no distillation, calling the same manifest updater used by those commands changes the empty-result note to “all captured sessions are distilled.” This can discourage needed processing and misrepresent absent knowledge. Track actual processing coverage independently of fact-store refresh time; do not claim all sessions are processed based solely on their creation timestamps. Graph identifies empty-result retrieval and handoff consumers and fourteen consumers of the preservation helper. Brain retrieved the original blind-spot requirement in semantic_brain_plan.md:1206, which asks for actual undigested-session coverage. Reproduction: `audit-coverage-repro.log`.

The same preservation helper drops `TokenUsage` while retaining the other prior-run metrics. A second assertion confirms token accounting disappears on administrative manifest rebuilds. Preserve the complete last-run evidence as a unit rather than manually copying an expanding list of fields.



## F29 — P2: Negative tree leaf limit crashes the CLI

`internal/cli/facts_tree.go:154` slices with the unvalidated `--leaves` value. `facts tree --leaves -1` on a nonempty branch panics instead of returning a flag error. The overlay reproduces this through the real root command and a normal stored fact. Validate numeric options before retrieval/rendering. Graph confirms the command-to-renderer path; Brain retrieval found general tree/expansion design but no reason to allow this input. Evidence: `audit-factinputs-repro.log`.

A separate, lower-priority parser robustness issue exists in `facts_expand.go:77`: reading a cache containing valid JSON `null` sets its map to nil, then the next successful expansion panics assigning into that map. The same overlay reproduces it. Normalize decoded cache state and handle malformed cache inputs deliberately. Graph traces persistent cache loading to facts eval; ordinary recall uses an in-memory empty-path cache.

### Comment quality: false certainty and repetition

`facts_integrity.go` spends its first 83 lines retelling corruption incidents before declaring a type, and repeats the same accounts on fields and individual branches. Its duplicated-ID warning asserts every duplicate replaced a different fact, although a duplicate may simply have been appended (the code later acknowledges that case). `facts_admin_cmd.go` and its flag-validation tests likewise repeat the claim that promoting into a nonexistent branch destroys facts, although the source branch remains and explicit branch lookup can access the new store. Keep the actionable validation and corruption checks; replace these narratives with concise, accurate invariants. `facts_sync_cmd.go:324` also leaves a stale reconcileLocalProposalQueue comment attached to readSharedFactHead.



## F30 — P2: Resolving a hosted proposal can modify a different local repository

`internal/cli/facts_proposals_cmd.go:323` invokes local settlement after a successful hosted resolution without passing or verifying the hosted repository identity. `pruneLocalProposalCopy` selects the current checkout solely from Options and matches content-derived fact IDs. Run `facts proposals apply ... --repo-id <other-repository>` from a checkout containing the same facts: the command supersedes that checkout's local fact too, even with no local shared-proposal entry. An end-to-end CLI overlay with the existing loopback fake reproduces the wrong local status change. Require an established mapping between the hosted target and local store before mirroring; otherwise report the hosted outcome without mutating an unrelated checkout. Graph traces the resolver into this helper. Brain retrieved the original local queue-pruning change but no cross-repository binding requirement. Evidence: `audit-proposalrepo-repro.log`.

Additional test-quality example: `facts_test.go:11` names path-order stability, but its first two calls pass paths in exactly the same order. Reverse one input to exercise the stated property. The alias-level merge tests largely repeat the merge-core tests; preserve CLI integration assertions when consolidating.



## F31 — P2 — Standard silver fact-evaluation output cannot be compared by default

`internal/cli/facts_eval.go:842–861` emits `labeled=false` and `provenance_silver_label` for fixed silver task labels. `facts_eval_compare.go:266–275` requires `labeled=true` and `explicit_label`, rejecting even a summary compared with itself as “different ground truths.” `history_eval.go:382–391` represents the same label grade differently and passes. This contradicts the comparator comment and the recorded same-truth/non-proof distinction. Normalize the representation/comparability of fixed labels independently from release evidence grade, and test the facts gen→eval→compare seam as well as history. Repro: `evidence/audit-eval-repro.log`, TestAuditSilverOutputComparison. Graph impact: comparator 1 direct + 5 transitive callers (`audit-impact-evallabels.json`). Brain: release-blockers.md R1 at retained line 50 and session history:6426eca537eeaecb0cb9865f line 3965 document the intended distinction; release_readiness_audit.md has conflicting older strict wording, so source plus reproduction establishes current behavior.



## F49 — P2: secret-field redaction misses common quoting formats
`redaction.go:18` assumes the secret name immediately precedes the separator and consumes only a non-whitespace value. Quoted JSON keys (`{"API_KEY":"audit_fake_credential_123456"}` and `{"password": "audit_fake_credential_123456"}`) and `PASSWORD='audit fake credential value'` survive unchanged. TestAuditQuotedJSONSecretSurvivesRedaction uses fabricated credentials only. This affects the pattern evidence egress boundary, drafts and other redacted artifacts. Handle quoted keys and quoted values, with tests against actual serialized evidence. Graph redactText: 44 direct/67 transitive callers. Brain reference/threat-model docs describe best-effort redaction; that limitation does not explain missing the routine formats for explicitly supported field names. Evidence audit-redact*.



## F50 — P2: failure-tail hook reads the wrong end of large logs
`hook_cmd.go:294–302` applies a 1 MiB LimitReader before taking the last 4096 bytes. For larger logs, the true final errors are never read; it instead matches the end of the first MiB. TestAuditHookDropsActualFailureTail proves a final failure marker disappears. Use bounded-memory tail buffering through EOF, with appropriate cancellation, or require and accurately document pre-truncated input. Graph and Brain evidence audit-hooktail*; reproduction in audit-redact-repro.log.

### More comment quality issues
`reconcile_test.go` TestParseReconcileActionsRejectsNaNConfidence describes a new-line confidence default but actually tests merge confidence zero. `reconcile.go` writeFactProposals says deduplication uses a triple, while dedupeProposals correctly uses five fields; the following 12-line repair narrative can be reduced to the shared identity invariant. `redaction.go` claims every evidence field passes through a no-secrets boundary more strongly than the implementation establishes.



## F51 — P2: NaN confidence bypasses review and fails only after writes
`distill_cmd.go:614` checks only <=0 and >1, admitting NaN; runDistillForBrain passes it into the threshold comparison. `TestAuditDistillNaNThresholdAppliesLowConfidence` reproduces automatic supersession at confidence 0.01 and then a manifest JSON encoding error for NaN, after the fact store has changed. Reject non-finite configuration at both CLI and engine boundaries before calls or writes; parser guards already do this for model-produced confidence. External reproduction uses the engine; CLI admission is established by the flag predicate. Graph runDistillForBrain covers the production CLI and library consumers. Evidence audit-distillnew* and audit-distill-impact/brain.



## F52 — P2: distillation replaces newer session manifests with its old snapshot
`distill_cmd.go:1284–1288` publishes the manifest loaded at the beginning of a potentially hours-long pass. The final writer lock protects only that write and does not merge changes since the earlier read. TestAuditDistillOverwritesNewSessionManifest writes a newly captured session under the same brain lock during an agent call; successful distillation removes it from the manifest. Reload the current manifest inside the final lock and update only the fact-source fields owned by this pass. Reproduction audit-distillnew*; Graph runDistillForBrain impact retained. Existing concurrent-writer tests cover facts but omit manifest sources.



## F53 — P2: proposal read errors become destructive queue replacement
`distill_cmd.go:1002–1017` logs loadFactProposals errors and proceeds with an empty prior queue. `writeFactProposals` then replaces or removes the old file. TestAuditDistillErasesMalformedProposalQueue shows a malformed existing queue deleted by a successful incremental distill. Refuse publication on unreadable queue state; preserve the evidence for repair. Graph loadFactProposals and runDistillForBrain impact retained. Evidence audit-distillnew* and audit-proposalread*.

### Distillation maintenance issues
- runDistillForBrain combines scheduling, extraction, reconciliation, cache migration, rebase, publication and reporting in roughly 540 lines with several large closures. Its concurrency fixes protect individual facts but the final manifest still has a stale-snapshot gap (F52); explicit phase/result types and a single publication transaction would make ownership reviewable. The pipeline's ordered dispatcher is justified by its deadlock invariant; preserve that invariant during any refactor.
- `distillSessionFingerprint` first says it hashes transcript path, then says it deliberately does not. `concurrency` refers to removed chunkPrefetcher. `saveDistillCache` calls failure non-fatal even though final flush returns it. `parseDocumentConversation` says tool outputs are scanned past, but ToolOutputs now materializes them.
- Numerous comments narrate previous failures and observed corpus sizes at length. Keep current invariants, compatibility boundaries and non-obvious scheduling rationale; move incident chronology to history/docs.



## F54 — P2: distill cache and proposal readers can block indefinitely on FIFOs
`distill_cmd.go` loadDistillCache and `reconcile.go` loadFactProposals call os.ReadFile directly, bypassing the bounded regular-file state reader immediately above the cache loader. TestAuditDistillAndProposalFIFOBlock confirms both block until a controlled writer arrives. The reads have no context or byte bound, and proposal reads also occur inside the brain writer lock. Use the existing safe state-reader boundary and preserve meaningful errors for non-rebuildable queue state. Graph cache loader 16 direct/51 transitive callers; proposal loader 27 direct/76 transitive. Evidence audit-statefifo*, audit-distillcache-impact and audit-proposalread-impact. Same boundary class as F37; consolidate in final prioritization without hiding affected consumers.

### Further distill test gaps
- TestExecDistillAgentTimesOutAndKillsTheProcess checks absence of a marker after about five seconds even though the marker is scheduled after 30 seconds; it does not establish the claimed lifetime property. The separate inherited-pipe test does verify wait duration and cleans up its child.
- TestForcedCappedDistillDoesNotStrandDeferredSessions uses recordingDistillRunner, which emits invalid two-level taxonomy `conventions.testing`. It proves cache visitation but creates no facts, despite claiming to prove preservation/recovery of dropped facts.
- TestInProcessDistillOptionsPassTheConcurrencyGuard describes both watcher and session-end coverage but asserts watcher options only.
- Brain doc:a01f73bf7558 explicitly says source owners must not independently replace shared manifest state (F52); doc:c31974aa0661 defines the low-confidence review contract (F51).

# Facts audit remediation

Branch codex/audit2-facts, base c6dff964. All eleven assigned findings reproduced and fixed.

| Finding | Change and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| F12 | Reject inactive records, self proposals, and unsupported actions before mutation. f12-red.log fails on old behavior; f12-green.log passes full factmerge/factsync suites. |
| F28 | Record LastDistilledAt only from actual distillation; preserve timestamp and token usage across manual updates. Empty results describe unknown coverage rather than inferring completeness from timestamps. f28-red.log and f28-green.log; manual timestamp/usage persistence regression included. Legacy manifests without a run timestamp remain explicitly unknown. |
| F29 | Reject negative tree leaves before resolving storage; rebuild null/malformed expansion cache maps. f29-red.log/f29-green.log, both text and JSON flag paths and persisted cache reuse. |
| F30 | Record successful HTTP sync's repo/API binding per branch; verify under local writer lock before mirroring hosted settlements. Missing or mismatched binding leaves facts/queue untouched and warns; successful real sync followed by proposal apply still mirrors. f30-red.log and f30-f31-green.log cover missing/different repo/different API and matching sync. |
| F31 | Compare actual fixed provenance-silver evaluator results without falsely upgrading their evidence grade. Partial/mixed silver remains noncomparable. f31-red.log/f30-f31-green.log includes real evaluator to comparator flow. |
| F49 | Redact JSON quoted secret keys and complete quoted values including whitespace, escapes and unterminated quotes. f49-f50-red.log/green.log. Clarify scope of redaction comment. |
| F50 | Stream through EOF with bounded retained memory, returning the actual final diagnostic after multi-megabyte output. f49-f50-red.log/green.log. |
| F51 | Reject NaN/infinite confidence before agents or writes; preserve existing default threshold handling. f51-f53-red.log/green.log. |
| F52 | Reload the manifest while holding the final write lock so concurrent session exports survive. f51-f53-red.log/green.log uses a real concurrent writer between extraction and publication. |
| F53 | Pre-read every dirty branch's proposal queue before any flush writes; return parse/read failures without destroying queue evidence. f51-f53-red.log/green.log preserves malformed original bytes. |
| F54 | Read distill cache/proposals through bounded hardened state reader, rejecting FIFO/symlink hazards. Rebuildable cache fails empty; durable queue errors propagate. f54-red.log/green.log controls and unblocks FIFO regression. |

Brain brief and retained rationale are in brief.json/history-context.json; source index is stale so retained context was used only for rationale. Graph impacts cover shared functions/types, with complete Go parsing and unrelated JSON diagnostics. Final graph-diff.json and commits.txt record semantic change and automatic checkpoint trailers.

facts-focused-all.log passes all matching distillation/proposal/tree/expansion/redaction/hook/blindspot/handoff/silver/comparison tests (40s). facts-race.log passes focused CLI/factmerge/factsync race checks. Repository vet and formatting passed. Full suite runs in full-go-test.log before publication. No production hosted service or real model was used in regressions. Windows FIFO coverage is intentionally excluded; shared reader's existing cross-platform tests remain.
"}

item.stdout:
## F18 — P2: three-name rename cycles resolve to a dead spelling

`internal/entityindex/query.go:444–448` compares only the two nodes adjacent to the cycle-closing edge. For the ordinary rename history A → B → C → A, resolving C compares B and C, ignores the newer A, and returns C. A full Build/Snapshot reproduction confirms this, with monotonically increasing commit timestamps. Resolve and SearchKeys feed entityHistory, so history results can identify a name that no longer exists. Select the current representative across the whole detected cycle, and test every entry point into cycles longer than two. Also revisit the fixed 16-hop cutoff for long valid chains.

Brain retrieved the recorded two-name-cycle fix (`8fd890bf1238`, retained history-gaps entry at line 971); this explains the recency tie-break but does not cover longer cycles. Graph impact lists Resolve and SearchKeys directly and entityHistory transitively. Evidence: audit-entitycycle-repro.log, audit-entitycycle_test.go, audit-impact-resolvealias.txt.



## F19 — P3: batch mutation complexity contradicts its O(1) claim

`internal/entityindex/state.go:70` scans all entries with maxTimestamp for every append, making N pushes onto the same entity list quadratic. The O(1)-per-mutation comment at lines 13–18 is false; tombstone filtering and set checks also retain linear scans. A focused benchmark on this machine took 0.346 ms for 1,000 pushes, 33.8 ms for 10,000 and 136 ms for 20,000. These are synthetic measurements of applyBatch, not end-to-end backfill timings. Cache each list's maximum timestamp while building position maps and update it after appends; state the actual remaining costs in the comment.

Graph impact identifies Build and migration with 33 direct/transitive callers. Brain retrieval returned the index architecture and historical fixes but no additional rationale for the remaining timestamp scans. Evidence: audit-batch-bench.log and audit-impact-applybatch.txt.



## F55 — P2: Warm entity cache bypasses the privacy read guard
`internal/cli/entities_cmd.go:563–623`: cache hits return session joins without loading the session privacy policy; failed rebuilds can also return the previous cache. A malformed tombstone policy still serves session linkage. Confirmed by TestAuditEntityWarmCacheIgnoresPrivacyFailure. Graph: loadEntityIndexView has 5 direct and 14 transitive callers, including history, show and provenance. Brain recall threat model doc:5d8c928b241b promises malformed policies fail closed. Apply the current read guard to cached session joins before returning them, including fallback paths. Evidence: audit-entityview*.



## F56 — P2: Entity join cache ignores newly ingested sessions
`internal/cli/entities_cmd.go:563–623`: validity checks only Git metadata tip and provider identity, although the derived cache also depends on the session manifest. Backfill before a manifest arrives, then ingest its checkpoint/session join: warm history still has no SessionIDs. Confirmed by TestAuditEntityCacheIgnoresNewSessionJoin. Include a session-generation dependency or refresh/filter joins separately. Same Graph reach and evidence as F55.



## F57 — P2: An unresolved branch silently disables entity-history filtering
`internal/cli/entities_cmd.go:360–422`: branchReachableCommits returns nil on Git failure; entityHistory interprets nil as unrestricted and labels the result with the requested branch. TestAuditEntityUnknownBranchUnfilters returns both commits for nonexistent branch. Graph helper has 2 direct and 3 transitive callers. Preserve a separate unknown/error state and return a clear error or explicit incomplete result. The provenance resolver intentionally permits unknown reachability; avoid changing that distinct contract accidentally. Evidence: audit-entityview-repro.log and audit-entitybranch-impact.json.



### F74 — P2: Removed workspace members remain in graph retrieval

`internal/cli/workspace.go:2818–2832` loads graph.json without checking current workspace membership or freshness. `runWorkspaceRemove` updates membership and clears freshness but leaves this cache intact. A temporary fixture creates a graph edge from local/a to local/b, removes local/b through the real command, verifies the manifest now has one member, then retrieves the removed member's edge through `retrieveWorkspaceGraphCrossEdges`. The edge has `VerificationRequired:false` and no caveat. `getWorkspaceLevelRecord` likewise reads the unchecked cache. Graph impact confirms those direct callers and `runWorkspaceRetrieve`/`runWorkspaceGet` transitively. Brain doc:b9772a45fcf5 states namespace isolation and current member-only search. Invalidate/revalidate graph membership at read time and bind cache freshness to member generations; invalidation alone must handle concurrent builders. Evidence: audit-workspace-cache-* and audit-workspace-graph-cache-impact.json. Related to F48, but this is a separate cache and read path.



### F75 — P2: A one-edge graph limit still allocates the complete cross-product

`internal/cli/workspace.go:1431` (`workspaceGraphCrossEdges`) constructs and sorts all cross-repository participant pairs before slicing to `limit`. Two repositories with 500 references each to one shared endpoint produce 250,000 temporary edges even when limit=1. Production-function benchmark (one iteration each, Apple M2): 100 per repo 8.19ms/16.63MB allocated; 300 per repo 82.75ms/150.68MB; 500 per repo 152.61ms/472.57MB. Allocation totals are cumulative per operation, not peak RSS. Multiple other cross-edge constructors follow this pattern. Graph impact identifies buildWorkspaceGraphPayload, runWorkspaceGraphManifest and writeWorkspaceGraphSnapshot. Brain doc:39cf02c0d61e describes workspace cross-repo impact/contract coordination; no reason found to retain the entire intermediate product for a bounded result. Use bounded top-k selection and indexed matching as appropriate; retain deterministic ranking. Evidence: audit-workspace-crossedges-bench.log and companion overlay/impact.

# Entity and workspace graph remediation

Branch codex/audit2-entities, base c6dff964. Seven findings fixed.

- F18: resolve an entire alias cycle by most recent member, deterministic lexical tie-break; valid long chains no longer truncate at 16. Full Build/Snapshot three-name regression and every cycle entry/100-hop chain pass. f18-red.log; f18-f19-final.log.
- F19: cache each list's maximum timestamp during a mutation batch; rebuild after fallback operations. Comments describe remaining tombstone/set scans. Reference-equivalence tests include timestamp overflow and fallback removal. Same benchmark 20,000 pushes fell from 242ms to 4.4ms locally (three iterations), f19-before.log/f19-after.log. Not an end-to-end indexing claim.
- F55/F56: refresh checkpoint/session joins using current guarded sources on every returned entity view, including warm and stale fallback caches. Privacy errors fail closed and late manifests appear without metadata-tip changes. f55-f57-red.log/green.log.
- F57: checked branch reachability returns errors for an unresolved explicit history filter. Existing provenance lookup retains its unknown-reachability contract through a wrapper. Full entity/provenance tests pass.
- F74: graph cache generation binds membership plus member manifests. Reads reject stale/legacy generations; a concurrent old builder cannot restore stale cache validity. Removal, changed-member generation, fresh positive, direct get and late builder regressions. f74-red.log; f74-compatibility.log. Synthetic existing graph fixtures now explicitly record their generation.
- F75: stream candidates into bounded deterministic top-k storage in all seven cross-edge constructors. Remove quadratic dedup maps on route/channel pairs. Reference ranked-pair test verifies prefix output across limits. The one-edge 500x500 benchmark drops cumulative allocations from 472,566,688 bytes to 123,456 bytes (single iteration); runtime from 116ms to 15.6ms. Input participant copies still scale linearly; enumeration of candidate pairs remains quadratic, retained output is bounded. f75-before.log/f75-after.log/f75-order.log.

Brain brief/retained history and all required Graph impacts retained beside this report. Brain is stale historical context only; Go Graph coverage is complete with unrelated JSON diagnostics. Full entity package and focused workspace/entity/provenance checks passed. Initial broad workspace run found one old synthetic graph fixture missing generation; corrected with focused compatibility validation. Focused race passed CLI/entityindex. Repository vet/format pass. Full suite and final Graph diff/commits recorded before publication by parent.

No actual privacy data, external model, network service, or paid evaluation used in reproductions. Graph cache invalidates conservatively on any member manifest change; cached graph availability resumes with refresh/rebuild. Optional tags and remote CI remain separate verification.

## F18 — P2: three-name rename cycles resolve to a dead spelling

`internal/entityindex/query.go:444–448` compares only the two nodes adjacent to the cycle-closing edge. For the ordinary rename history A → B → C → A, resolving C compares B and C, ignores the newer A, and returns C. A full Build/Snapshot reproduction confirms this, with monotonically increasing commit timestamps. Resolve and SearchKeys feed entityHistory, so history results can identify a name that no longer exists. Select the current representative across the whole detected cycle, and test every entry point into cycles longer than two. Also revisit the fixed 16-hop cutoff for long valid chains.

Brain retrieved the recorded two-name-cycle fix (`8fd890bf1238`, retained history-gaps entry at line 971); this explains the recency tie-break but does not cover longer cycles. Graph impact lists Resolve and SearchKeys directly and entityHistory transitively. Evidence: audit-entitycycle-repro.log, audit-entitycycle_test.go, audit-impact-resolvealias.txt.



## F19 — P3: batch mutation complexity contradicts its O(1) claim

`internal/entityindex/state.go:70` scans all entries with maxTimestamp for every append, making N pushes onto the same entity list quadratic. The O(1)-per-mutation comment at lines 13–18 is false; tombstone filtering and set checks also retain linear scans. A focused benchmark on this machine took 0.346 ms for 1,000 pushes, 33.8 ms for 10,000 and 136 ms for 20,000. These are synthetic measurements of applyBatch, not end-to-end backfill timings. Cache each list's maximum timestamp while building position maps and update it after appends; state the actual remaining costs in the comment.

Graph impact identifies Build and migration with 33 direct/transitive callers. Brain retrieval returned the index architecture and historical fixes but no additional rationale for the remaining timestamp scans. Evidence: audit-batch-bench.log and audit-impact-applybatch.txt.



## F55 — P2: Warm entity cache bypasses the privacy read guard
`internal/cli/entities_cmd.go:563–623`: cache hits return session joins without loading the session privacy policy; failed rebuilds can also return the previous cache. A malformed tombstone policy still serves session linkage. Confirmed by TestAuditEntityWarmCacheIgnoresPrivacyFailure. Graph: loadEntityIndexView has 5 direct and 14 transitive callers, including history, show and provenance. Brain recall threat model doc:5d8c928b241b promises malformed policies fail closed. Apply the current read guard to cached session joins before returning them, including fallback paths. Evidence: audit-entityview*.



## F56 — P2: Entity join cache ignores newly ingested sessions
`internal/cli/entities_cmd.go:563–623`: validity checks only Git metadata tip and provider identity, although the derived cache also depends on the session manifest. Backfill before a manifest arrives, then ingest its checkpoint/session join: warm history still has no SessionIDs. Confirmed by TestAuditEntityCacheIgnoresNewSessionJoin. Include a session-generation dependency or refresh/filter joins separately. Same Graph reach and evidence as F55.



## F57 — P2: An unresolved branch silently disables entity-history filtering
`internal/cli/entities_cmd.go:360–422`: branchReachableCommits returns nil on Git failure; entityHistory interprets nil as unrestricted and labels the result with the requested branch. TestAuditEntityUnknownBranchUnfilters returns both commits for nonexistent branch. Graph helper has 2 direct and 3 transitive callers. Preserve a separate unknown/error state and return a clear error or explicit incomplete result. The provenance resolver intentionally permits unknown reachability; avoid changing that distinct contract accidentally. Evidence: audit-entityview-repro.log and audit-entitybranch-impact.json.



### F74 — P2: Removed workspace members remain in graph retrieval

`internal/cli/workspace.go:2818–2832` loads graph.json without checking current workspace membership or freshness. `runWorkspaceRemove` updates membership and clears freshness but leaves this cache intact. A temporary fixture creates a graph edge from local/a to local/b, removes local/b through the real command, verifies the manifest now has one member, then retrieves the removed member's edge through `retrieveWorkspaceGraphCrossEdges`. The edge has `VerificationRequired:false` and no caveat. `getWorkspaceLevelRecord` likewise reads the unchecked cache. Graph impact confirms those direct callers and `runWorkspaceRetrieve`/`runWorkspaceGet` transitively. Brain doc:b9772a45fcf5 states namespace isolation and current member-only search. Invalidate/revalidate graph membership at read time and bind cache freshness to member generations; invalidation alone must handle concurrent builders. Evidence: audit-workspace-cache-* and audit-workspace-graph-cache-impact.json. Related to F48, but this is a separate cache and read path.

`internal/cli/workspace.go:1431` (`workspaceGraphCrossEdges`) constructs and sorts all cross-repository participant pairs before slicing to `limit`. Two repositories with 500 references each to one shared endpoint produce 250,000 temporary edges even when limit=1. Production-function benchmark (one iteration each, Apple M2): 100 per repo 8.19ms/16.63MB allocated; 300 per repo 82.75ms/150.68MB; 500 per repo 152.61ms/472.57MB. (file: r5/documents/26.909.12148/skills/documents/SKILL.md)

Do not use for one-off creation from an existing template. (file: r5/template-creator/26.909.12148/skills/template-creator/SKILL.md)

# Independent entities/workspace review and repairs

Reviewed baseline 8922a654483309f6d60cf54e22d01b2cd0adae57, branch codex/audit2-entities. Worker session 01a0bb4c-42b6-7e13-b6e4-f349a323d9db.

Two actionable regressions confirmed and repaired (also independently reported by Cursor):

1. F75 bounded top-k used rank equality as identity. Canonically equivalent routes or duplicate channel participants with different occurrence counts consumed multiple slots for the same edge and displaced distinct pairs. The retained slice now deduplicates by the exact logical fields used for edge IDs and keeps the strongest candidate. No all-candidate identity map is introduced; retained edge storage stays O(limit). Route and channel tests fail on the baseline; channel test exercises both score orders.
2. F74 generation computation returned a member manifest error before the established per-repository degraded-result loop. A single malformed member prevented healthy graph edges from being built or read. Generation now includes an unavailable-member marker; the builder continues to report the individual failure. An integration test indexes three repositories, corrupts one manifest, verifies two healthy members and usable persisted edges, then restores the third manifest and verifies invalidation.

Red evidence: review-regressions-red.log (route and degraded member); channel-red.log (Go overlay uses untouched baseline source). Green evidence: review-regressions-green.log. Broader focused/race and vet logs recorded alongside this report. No production changes after those test invocations began.

Bounded allocation benchmark remains 123456 bytes and 6 allocations for 500x500 participant pairs, limit 1 (single iteration). It does not measure peak RSS or claim subquadratic pair enumeration. The duplicate lookup scans only retained candidates; early pruning avoids scans for candidates no better than the current worst.

No additional actionable defect found in alias cycle or batch timestamp changes. Alias resolution selects the latest touched cycle member, with deterministic tie-breaks; the mutation builder records reverse history only for the rename destination. Long chains and cycle-prefix behavior are covered by existing regressions. Entity cached session bindings use the guarded current session join on each return path. This is a bounded review, not proof of absence of other defects.

Brain availability/capabilities were established earlier this session; brief and retained rationale are saved here. Retrieved material was general architecture, not an authoritative explanation for these specific changes. Current source and executed regressions establish the findings. Graph impact: keepWorkspaceGraphEdge has 7 direct/35 total callers; workspaceGraphGeneration has 12 total callers. Further alias/applyBatch/loadEntityIndexView impacts retained. Go coverage available; Graph reports unrelated large JSON diagnostics and an informational unmerged data-flow evidence warning, which does not alter call relations. Full repository test gate and publication are parent-owned.
EOF
